$comment: MCR IMAGE PIN REGISTRY — every mcr.microsoft.com image a Loom DEPLOY PATH pulls,
with its resolved manifest digest (FINISHLINE C18).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. MIR0 (scripts/ci/check-upstream-image-mirror.mjs, issue #2682)
polices third-party registries — docker.io, ghcr.io, quay.io — and DELIBERATELY skips
mcr.microsoft.com because MCR is Microsoft first-party and is reachable from every
boundary Loom deploys into, so the ACR-mirror requirement does not apply. But the skip
was total: nothing at all looked at an MCR ref. Four of them floated `:latest`, one of
them on a DEFAULT-ON path (dabRuntimeEnabled = true), and all of them were baked into
the shipped ARM artifact apps/fiab-console/deploy-templates/main.json. A floating tag
means two deploys of the SAME commit can produce different running bytes, which
falsifies the build-marker SHA as an identifier of what is running.
THE PIN. Every ref is written in bicep as `<repo>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` (or
`<repo>@sha256:<digest>` where upstream publishes no version tag). The tag stays for
human readability; the digest is what the runtime resolves. Enforced by
scripts/ci/check-mcr-image-pins.mjs (MCR0), which keys on the SAFE property — a digest
is PRESENT and matches this file — not on the string ':latest'. Keying on ':latest'
would go quiet the moment someone wrote ':2.0.9' with no digest, which is still
mutable: MCR republishes rolling tags like `4-python3.11` and `2.0` in place.
TO BUMP A VERSION. Change `tag` AND `digest` together here, change the bicep ref to
match byte-for-byte, and re-run `az bicep build` so the compiled template moves with it.
Resolve the digest with:
bash scripts/ci/resolve-mcr-digest.sh <repo> <tag>
inlineDigest:false — the ONLY escape hatch. It means the consuming ARM resource type is
not known to accept a digest reference, so the bicep ref carries an immutable-by-
convention version tag instead. It is strictly weaker than a digest and must carry a
written reason. The digest is still recorded here so drift is detectable.
SCOPE. Deploy-TIME pulls only — an image a running Container App / Container Apps Job /
Container Instance / AML environment pulls. Images an apps/*/Dockerfile builds FROM are
pulled server-side by `az acr build` and baked into a Loom-owned image; those are
covered by LIC0 + the base-image CVE gate.

images.note: `:latest` resolved to this SAME digest on 2026-08-08, so the pin is byte-identical to what the estate was already running — it only stops the bits moving under a fixed SHA.
consumers: platform/fiab/bicep/modules/admin-plane/dab-runtime.bicep (dabImage) — DAB preview runtime, DEFAULT-ON (main.bicep dabRuntimeEnabled = true)
deploy/bicep/DLZ/modules/data-api-builder.bicep (dabImage) — the tutorial/example DLZ module operators deploy by hand (docs/tutorials/11-data-api-builder)

images.note: `2.0` is a ROLLING tag — CBL-Mariner republishes it in place for CVE rebases. Not `:latest`, but not immutable either; this is exactly the case a ':latest'-keyed guard would have missed.
`4-python3.11` is a ROLLING tag — the Functions base images are rebuilt in place on every runtime patch.
consumers: platform/fiab/bicep/modules/admin-plane/udf-runtime.bicep (udfImage) — User Data Functions execution host, DEFAULT-ON

images.note: Upstream publishes NO tag but `latest` (verified: GET https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/azuredocs/aci-helloworld/tags/list returns exactly ["latest"]). There is no version tag to fall back to, so the ref is digest-only.
consumers: platform/fiab/bicep/modules/deploy-planner/container-instances.bicep (image) — the sample group the Container Instances navigator lists/starts/stops; opt-in (containerInstancesEnabled = false)

images.inlineDigestBlockedBy: Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/environments/versions documents `image` only as "Name of the image that will be used for the environment" and no Learn page states that a digest reference is accepted; a wrong guess here breaks AML environment creation on a DEFAULT-ON path (mlWorkspaceEnabled = true) and cannot be tested without a live AML deploy. Pinned to the dated AzureML base-image tag instead, which AzureML publishes immutably (new bases get a NEW date, the old date is never republished). Weaker than a digest — the digest is recorded here so drift is still detectable. Re-open when the digest form is confirmed on a live deploy.
images.note: `:latest` resolved to this SAME digest on 2026-08-08, so the pin is byte-identical to what the estate was already running.
